post.description:
If its type reuses duplicates and you can read one with the same identity, that one
is returned (200, ``reused``) and added to the project, instead of a copy. If its type
warns about duplicates, the request is refused (409, ``duplicate``) unless
``allow_duplicate`` is set.

Entities you can read that match every filter given: a type (with its subtypes), a
project, archived or not, text in their HRID or title (``q``), membership of a
``collection``, and ``where``, conditions on the type's fields. Sorted by ``sort``
(then by ID), oldest first without one.

Each kind of field takes its own operators, and every field takes ``is_set``:

- string: ``eq``, ``ne``, ``in``, ``contains``, ``starts_with`` (any case)
- text: ``contains``, ``matches`` (its words: ``"kinase -fragment"``, ``""active site""``)
- enum, reference: ``eq``, ``ne``, ``in`` (references by ID or HRID)
- int, float, quantity, date, datetime: ``eq``, ``ne``, ``in``, ``lt``, ``lte``, ``gt``,
  ``gte`` (quantities in the field's unit, or ``{"value": 50, "unit": "kDa"}``)
- bool: ``eq``; file: ``eq``, ``ne``; list: ``has``

``ne`` matches entities without a value too. Every entity also has ``hrid``, ``type``,
``owner_project``, ``created_by``, ``created_at``, ``updated_at`` and ``archived_at``.
A search may run for 15 seconds: conditions on indexed fields keep it fast.

service account you choose (`run_as`), on your authority: either way you must be able to
run its action here. Only in the web app: no token, and so no agent, can turn one on.

A queued run is cancelled at once; a running one is asked to stop, and its worker ends
it. Whoever may launch the run's tier in its project may cancel it.

get.description:
The entities it created, updated or reused, that you can read, in the order it
wrote them.

post.description:
Queue a run that reproduces this one exactly (ADR 0057): the same plugin commit,
action as launched, params, plugin settings, inputs at the revisions it read, and seed.
It writes nothing: when it ends, `reproduction` says whether its results are the same.
A run that reused another's results is reproduced as that one. Whoever may launch its
tier in its project may reproduce it; it's refused (409) when this deployment runs
other code for its plugin.

Once every part has arrived. Iki then checks the bytes (202), and the upload becomes
ready, or fails if they don't match its SHA-256. Finishing it again changes nothing.
New URLs, when the earlier ones expired before every part was sent.

By its ID or HRID (WF-000123). Its live updates come from

post.description:
No further step starts, and its running steps' runs are cancelled, as
`POST /runs/{ref}/cancel` would. It ends cancelled once they have.

A new workflow run, started by you, of the workflow as it was, on the same inputs (as
they are now) and params, as GitHub re-runs failed jobs. Steps that succeeded are carried
over with their runs and results; the rest run again, and approvals are asked again. Only
a workflow run that failed or was cancelled is re-run, by whoever may start it.
post.summary: Re-run a workflow run from its failed steps

post.description:
The step starts, as whoever started the workflow. Someone with its approval's role in
the project may, other than whoever started it, and only in the web app.

The step doesn't run, and the workflow fails; whoever started it is told why. As
approving, someone with the role, other than whoever started it, in the web app.

get.description: Every workflow installed plugins provide, in name order.

post.description:
Start a run of the workflow. Everything it can be is checked first: your role for
each step's tier, that each step's action can run here, its inputs and its params. Its
first steps are launched before it answers; each later one once those it takes from
have succeeded.
